passages.title: Cyrus and Artaxerxes
passages.author: Xenophon
passages.blurb: Darius dies; his sons Artaxerxes and Cyrus become rivals. Plain narrative prose, the classic first Xenophon.

passages.title: Θάλαττα, θάλαττα!
passages.author: Xenophon
passages.blurb: The Ten Thousand reach the mountain and see the sea. Short sentences, vivid action.

passages.title: The news reaches Athens
passages.author: Xenophon
passages.blurb: Night in Athens as the Paralus brings word of the disaster at Aegospotami. Longer sentences.

passages.title: Why this war mattered
passages.author: Thucydides
passages.blurb: The historian introduces himself and his subject. Dense, famous, and slow going: a stretch text.

passages.title: Socrates wakes in prison
passages.author: Plato
passages.blurb: Crito arrives before dawn; short conversational exchanges, ideal for hearing question intonation.

passages.title: Down to the Piraeus
passages.author: Plato
passages.blurb: The famous opening: a festival, a walk home, and Polemarchus' slave tugging Socrates' cloak.

passages.title: The charge against Socrates
passages.author: Xenophon
passages.blurb: Xenophon wonders how Athens was persuaded to condemn Socrates. The same page as the Loeb OCR test.

passages.title: Socrates begins his defence
passages.author: Plato
passages.blurb: "How you were affected by my accusers, I do not know." Rhetorical, balanced clauses.

passages.title: Ouranos, Gaia and the Titans
passages.author: Apollodorus
passages.blurb: The first gods and the first family quarrel, in the simplest prose in this library.

passages.title: Prometheus steals fire
passages.author: Apollodorus
passages.blurb: Prometheus makes men from clay, steals fire in a fennel stalk, and pays for it on the Caucasus.

passages.title: Athena and Poseidon contend for Athens
passages.author: Apollodorus
passages.blurb: A salt spring, an olive tree, and the naming of the city.

passages.title: The birth of Heracles
passages.author: Apollodorus
passages.blurb: Zeus, Alcmene, a night made three times long, and two snakes in the cradle.
